clue.text: There's me, so robust in retrospect an example of longevity

parts.note: taken as written
so and thus both mean in this way, therefore

indicators.note: looking back in time, so the word for robust is written backwards

parts.note: robust means hale, healthy and strong

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that their sturdy constitution, looking back, makes them a model of long life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retrospect' turns HALE into ELAH, which ends the answer after ME and THUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical patriarch said to have lived 969 years is the proverbial figure of great age.

clue.text: Port for yours truly, honey

parts.note: the speaker referring to themselves, me
mel is Latin for honey, as in mellifluous

explanation.surface: A letter signed 'yours truly' to a sweetheart called honey, about a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: MEL is Latin for honey, used in pharmacy names.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic seaport now called Klaipeda in Lithuania was formerly known by this German name.

clue.text: Pay-as-you-vote device ?

parts.note: split as pay-charge plus polling cabin, where a vote would cost money

explanation.walkthrough: A toll is a charge you pay and a polling booth is where you vote; joined, they name the kiosk at a toll road.
explanation.definitionFit: The kiosk where road users pay a charge combines a charge and a voting cabin.

clue.text: Lime Street, where Mark made a purchase

definitions.meaning: the great Berlin boulevard whose German name means under the lime trees
the mark was the German currency, so it bought things there

explanation.walkthrough: Lime Street is also a Liverpool station, a false trail; the German name means 'under the limes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Berlin's famous avenue is named for its lime trees, and German marks were spent in its shops.

clue.text: Springlike in Castile

indicators.note: the answer lies in the letters of the word that follows, rearranged

explanation.surface: Something resembling spring found in a Spanish region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' asks for the answer to be found in the letters of CASTILE, rearranged; it is not a hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretchy material springs back to shape like a coiled spring.

clue.text: Con makes Vere sad

indicators.note: the two words are made into a new word by rearranging their letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A swindle leaves a man called Vere unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' is not a swindle but the opposite of 'pro', meaning against; 'makes' signals rearranging VERE SAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Con, as in pros and cons, means against or opposed, which is what hostile conditions are.

clue.text: Author skipper

definitions.meaning: Charles ..., the English essayist who wrote as Elia
a young sheep, which skips about in spring

explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb is a famous essayist, and a young sheep is known for skipping in the fields.

clue.text: Robin " whom I wished to see, Wished for to hear "

definitions.text: Robin " whom I wished to see, Wished for to hear "

parts.words: Robin " whom I wished to see, Wished for to hear "
parts.note: a quotation from the old Irish-Scottish song addressed to Robin, whose surname completes the title

explanation.walkthrough: The ballad 'Robin ...' contains the lines 'He whom I wished to see, Wished for to hear'.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname completes the title of the old song 'Robin Adair' from which the lines come.

clue.text: For an energizing loaf ?

parts.note: split as buck, to liven up, plus a grain for bread

explanation.walkthrough: To buck up is to energize, and wheat makes a loaf, so the grain sounds like bread that perks you up.
explanation.definitionFit: A grain plant used for flour combines words for 'enliven' and bread-making corn.

clue.text: A wiry lad heard humming early in the morning

definitions.text: A wiry lad heard humming early in the morning

parts.words: A wiry lad heard humming early in the morning
parts.note: wiry suggests a mains-powered appliance, and a lad is a young shaver

explanation.walkthrough: A young boy is called a 'young shaver', and the wired appliance hums as men shave in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A mains-powered razor hums in the bathroom at the start of the day.

clue.text: A uniform but irregular force

parts.note: a body of citizen soldiers who wear uniform but are not part of the regular army

explanation.surface: A contradiction: a body in uniform that is nonetheless irregular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irregular' is not untidy here: it means not belonging to the regular, professional army.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen army raised in emergencies is uniformed yet outside the regular forces.

clue.text: Of electric or river current ?

parts.note: relating to galvanic electricity named after Alessandro Volta, or to the Volta river of West Africa

explanation.walkthrough: The word describes electric current produced chemically, named after the physicist Volta; the question mark plays on the Volta, a river in Ghana.
explanation.definitionFit: Galvanic electricity is named after Volta, who built the first battery, and the Volta is also a Ghanaian river.

clue.text: Freer in the air of war

definitions.meaning: the Consolidated B-24, an American heavy bomber of the Second World War

explanation.definitionFit: A rescuer who frees people shares the name of a famous wartime American bomber aircraft.

clue.text: A crew cut for a poet

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are cut up and reshuffled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A short-cropped haircut suggested as a style for a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A crew cut' reads as a haircut, but 'cut' tells you to rearrange A CREW.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Carew was a Cavalier poet of the court of Charles I.

clue.text: It can make one a bell-hop

definitions.text: It can make one a bell-hop

parts.words: It can make one a bell-hop
parts.note: a device whose ringing sends someone hopping to answer it

explanation.walkthrough: A bell-hop is a hotel porter, but here it is anyone who hops up when the bell rings.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone rings, and its bell makes the hearer jump up to answer.

clue.text: In advance yielded, but came out on top

parts.note: pre- means before, in advance
to vail is an old verb meaning to lower or yield

explanation.surface: Someone who gave way beforehand still ended up winning.
explanation.walkthrough: VAIL, to lower or yield, is an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: To come out on top is to win through, to triumph.

clue.text: Jolly Bros., merchants, of City Square

definitions.text: Jolly Bros., merchants, of City Square

parts.words: Jolly Bros., merchants, of City Square
parts.note: the cheerful twin merchant brothers in Dickens's Nicholas Nickleby, whose counting-house is in a City square

explanation.walkthrough: In Nicholas Nickleby the benevolent twins Charles and Ned run their business from a quiet square in the City of London; 'Jolly' hints at their name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens named his good-hearted merchant twins for their cheerful nature.

clue.text: Non-Greek, non-Roman, but perhaps a pub-crawling Scot?

parts.note: going from bar to bar
Ian is the Scottish form of John, a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: Asking whether a foreigner might be a Scotsman on a drinking tour.
explanation.walkthrough: A pub-crawl goes from bar to bar; IAN is a stock Scottish name.
explanation.definitionFit: To the Greeks and Romans anyone outside their civilisation was an uncivilised foreigner.

clue.text: Miss Newcome " distressed " by the king of Mercia

parts.note: Ethel Newcome, heroine of Thackeray's novel The Newcomes
read as dis-tressed, without tresses, hence hairless

explanation.surface: A young lady from a Victorian novel is upset by an Anglo-Saxon king.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks round 'distressed' signal reading it as 'without tresses', i.e. hairless.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethelbald ruled the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia in the eighth century.

clue.text: For which the herbalist might prescribe myosotis ?

definitions.text: For which the herbalist might prescribe myosotis ?

parts.words: For which the herbalist might prescribe myosotis ?
parts.note: myosotis is the forget-me-not, so it is jokily prescribed for loss of memory

explanation.walkthrough: Myosotis is the botanical name for the forget-me-not, so it would be the herbal cure for forgetfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory would be treated by a plant whose name says 'forget me not'.

clue.text: Why elderly husbands are not free-handed

definitions.text: Why elderly husbands are not free-handed

parts.words: Why elderly husbands are not free-handed
parts.note: elderly husbands recall Darby of Darby and Joan, and not free-handed means handcuffed

explanation.walkthrough: Darby and Joan are the proverbial devoted old couple; the old slang word for handcuffs looks like 'Darby's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang for handcuffs, which leave the wearer without free hands.

clue.text: Painter of landscape — a waterfowl right in the middle

indicators.note: the letter for right goes into the centre of the bird's name

parts.note: a coot is a black water bird

explanation.surface: A landscape painter depicts a water bird set right at the centre of the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the middle' places R between the two Os of COOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Camille Corot was a French painter celebrated for his landscapes.

clue.text: Eloquent rodman

parts.note: the brother of Moses who spoke for him and whose rod budded and became a serpent

explanation.walkthrough: In Exodus he is Moses's fluent spokesman, and his rod turns into a serpent before Pharaoh.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's high priest was chosen to speak for Moses and carried a miraculous rod.

clue.text: Snappish as a terrier

definitions.meaning: like a terrier, a dog bred to catch rodents

explanation.definitionFit: Irritable people are called this, and a terrier bred to hunt vermin is full of rodents' foes.

clue.text: Former premier and Rugbeian give direction

parts.note: Lord North, British prime minister during the American War of Independence
Harry East, Tom Brown's friend at Rugby School in Tom Brown's Schooldays

explanation.surface: An ex-prime minister and an old boy of Rugby School give instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: A Rugbeian is a pupil of Rugby School, the English public school; East is Tom Brown's chum there in the Victorian novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The compass point midway between two cardinal points is a direction.

clue.text: 17'slack?

parts.note: the clue at 17 reads ... as hairless, so what is lacking is a lock of hair

explanation.walkthrough: 17 across splits 'distressed' as without tresses; this is what is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A long lock of hair is what someone hairless has lost.

clue.text: Learning methods of communication

definitions.meaning: scholarship, as in a man of ...

explanation.definitionFit: Literary scholarship is called this, as are written messages posted to someone.

clue.text: Singer at his best — list !

definitions.meaning: a singer in good voice is said to be on form vocally
an itemised bill of goods supplied

explanation.definitionFit: A singer on top form is said to be 'in voice', and an itemised bill is a list of charges.

clue.text: " Shuts up the story of our" (Raleigh)

definitions.text: " Shuts up the story of our" (Raleigh)

parts.words: " Shuts up the story of our" (Raleigh)
parts.note: the missing word from Raleigh's poem Even Such Is Time, written before his execution

explanation.walkthrough: Raleigh's lines run: 'Who in the dark and silent grave, When we have wandered all our ways, Shuts up the story of our ...', rhyming with 'ways'.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem says Time ends the tale of our lives, the span of time we live.

clue.text: Had Pegasus been a Percheron, might he have been classed as one of these ?

definitions.text: Had Pegasus been a Percheron, might he have been classed as one of these ?

parts.words: Had Pegasus been a Percheron, might he have been classed as one of these ?
parts.note: a Percheron is a draught horse, but split it reads 'percher on', and a winged percher would be a perching bird

explanation.walkthrough: A Percheron is a heavy French cart-horse; the clue hears it as 'percher-on', and the perching birds form a large order.
explanation.definitionFit: The order of perching songbirds is named for sparrows and their habit of gripping a branch.
